findings.title: SQL injection via f-string in search_orders_advanced
findings.explanation: search_orders_advanced builds SQL with f"... LIKE '%{query}%'" where query comes from /orders/search2 q param. Attacker can inject e.g. ' OR '1'='1 to bypass filter, exfiltrate or modify data.

evidence.why: User input interpolated directly into SQL via f-string, no parameterization

findings.suggestion: Use parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT ... WHERE status LIKE ?", (f"%{query}%",))

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-user order search exposes all orders
findings.explanation: orders_search2 drops the user scoping used by orders_search and calls search_orders_advanced which queries all users' orders. Any caller can enumerate all orders, broken access control.

evidence.why: New route takes only q with no User auth, unlike /orders/search
Function explicitly searches across all users orders by status

findings.suggestion: Require authenticated User and scope query by user_name like search_orders does.

findings.title: Hardcoded AWS secret in source
findings.explanation: RECEIPT_AWS_KEY is hardcoded in shop/uploads.py. Committed secrets leak via repo history and are hard to rotate.

evidence.why: AWS secret assigned as literal in source file

findings.suggestion: Remove literal; load from environment or secret manager and never commit.
